title: Managed retreat planning frameworks
bottleneck: Sea-level rise will eventually force relocation of coastal communities, but managed retreat remains politically toxic and practically unplanned: no country has a fair, funded framework for deciding who moves, when, who pays, and where they go. Property markets and insurance continue to price coastal real estate as if the sea were not rising, and post-disaster rebuilding usually reconstructs the same vulnerability. The science of local sea-level timing exists; the governance does not.
why_it_blocks: Unplanned retreat means the poorest move first with the least support while the wealthy rebuild on subsidized insurance — climate displacement without justice or efficiency. Delay converts an orderly transition into chaotic, crisis-driven flight.
current_state: A few jurisdictions — parts of the US, Fiji, New Zealand — have piloted buyout and relocation programs, but they cover tiny populations relative to the hundreds of millions in exposed coastal zones. The policy toolkit is essentially experimental.
